problem_motivation.content: Need to study synthesis possibilities of HfNbTaTiZr HEA from powders as powder metallurgy is a perspective technique.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Powder metallurgy is a perspective technique of alloy synthesis and therefore in this work the possibilities of synthesis of HfNbTaTiZr HEA from powders were studied.

problem_motivation.content: There is a need to examine various techniques for removing residual porosity in HfNbTaTiZr alloy prepared by powder metallurgy.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Therefore in this work various techniques of removing residual porosity were examined

prior_approach.content: Arc or induction melting is identified as the most frequent synthesis method for HEAs.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The most frequent method of HEA synthesis is arc or induction melting.

prior_approach.content: HfNbTaTiZr alloy is typically prepared using an arc melting process.
prior_approach.evidence_span: This alloy is usually prepared by an arc melting process

prior_approach.content: Previous literature reports a specific cooling rate threshold for retaining single-phase random solid solution.
prior_approach.evidence_span: It was reported by Senkov et al. [ [22] ] that cooling rate higher than 15 °C/min is sufficient for retaining single phase random solid solution at this alloy.

prior_approach.content: Prior work established that high entropy alloys can exhibit higher hardness due to atomic size fluctuations hindering dislocation motion.
prior_approach.evidence_span: It was reported that the high entropy effect may result into higher hardness since various radii of atoms occupying randomly lattice sites cause random fluctuations of potential energy landscape, which hinders motion of dislocations [ [2] ].

prior_limitation.content: The swaging method with titanium alloy envelope fails to produce a fully dense alloy due to cracking.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: This method does not result in a full density alloy due to cracking during swaging.

prior_limitation.content: Spark plasma sintering of mechanically alloyed powders produces a fully dense specimen that is brittle.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed powders resulted in a fully dense but brittle specimen.

prior_limitation.content: Arc-melted alloys suffer from coarse dendritic microstructures which lead to phase separation.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: The dendritic microstructure may lead to phase separation (a mixture of two phases with slightly different chemical composition) due to variation of chemical composition in dendrite and interdendritic regions

prior_limitation.content: Powder metallurgy processed HEAs have residual porosity that significantly deteriorates mechanical properties.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: On the other hand, residual porosity present after sintering deteriorates the mechanical properties of HEAs significantly

prior_limitation.content: Initial powders used in powder metallurgy have large active surfaces, making them vulnerable to oxidation.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Moreover the initial powders have large active surfaces and could therefore be vulnerable to oxidation

rejected_alternative.content: The authors did not rely solely on hot compression tests to represent real forging processes because the two differ significantly.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: However, it should be pointed out that the hot compression tests and real forging processes may significantly differ from each other

rejected_alternative.content: The authors chose not to use CIP followed by HIP for HPT processing because that route produces samples unsuitable for the required strain, whereas the alternative method of sintering/swaging allows for the fabrication of small discs that can be strained by HPT.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Contrary to CIP followed by HIP, sintering (or swaging), which is suitable for fabrication of large samples, produces relatively small disc shape samples with diameter of 20 mm and thickness of a few mm. Such samples can be strained by high pressure torsion (HPT)

causal_claim.content: Hot swaging increased hardness due to dislocation strengthening, though the measurement may be unreliable due to specimen cracking.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Table 2 shows that hardness increased during hot swaging to more than 400 HV10, indicating strengthening of the material by dislocations introduced by swaging.

causal_claim.content: Sintering caused grain growth, which reduced dislocation density and increased the positron lifetime.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The sintering caused narrowing of XRD profiles, which indicated grain growth occurring during sintering. LT investigations revealed that sintering reduced dislocation density and also the concentration of misfit defects, which was indicated by increases of τ 2 towards the value of ≈180 ps, typical for dislocations in HfNbTaTiZr alloy [ [38] ]. The latter effect was obviously caused by grain growth during sintering.

causal_claim.content: HPT processing resulted in the formation of a high density of dislocations exceeding 5 × 10^14 m^-2, evidenced by saturated positron trapping.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This testifies that virtually all positrons were annihilated in a trapped state in dislocations (so called saturated positron trapping). Hence, one can conclude that HPT processing resulted in formation of a high density of dislocations exceeding 5 × 10 14 m −2 .

causal_claim.content: HPT straining caused an increase in hardness for both sample types.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In Figure 8 one can see that HPT straining increased hardness of both MA-SPS-HPT and AT-SPS-HPT samples.

causal_claim.content: The presence of oxides and oxygen caused brittleness and prevented single-phase formation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Oxygen incorporated into the HfNbTaTiZr samples caused deterioration of mechanical properties (embrittlement) and prevented formation of a single phase random solid solution.

mechanism_principle.content: The increase in oxygen content during processing is attributed to the high surface area of nanocrystalline particles during ball milling.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Oxygen was incorporated into the MA powder obviously during high energy ball milling due to high surface area of nanocrystalline powder particles.

mechanism_principle.content: The presence of two chemically different bcc phases with slightly different lattice parameters causes misfit defects at their interfaces.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since bcc1 and bcc2 phases had slightly different lattice parameters, the discontinuity of lattice planes resulted in the formation of misfit defects at interfaces between these two phases [ [27] ].

mechanism_principle.content: The high oxygen content in the MA-SPS specimen is attributed to powder contamination with large active surface area and reactivity.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This was probably caused by a significant oxygen contamination of powders with large active surface area. This was possibly due to a long milling time and residual oxygen present in the milling atmosphere (Ar), and high reactivity of some elements with the oxygen (e.g., Ti, Hf)

mechanism_principle.content: The single-phase structure is caused by a high cooling rate dissolving secondary phases.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Single phase random solid solution is caused by relatively high cooling rate after SPS processing at high temperature of 1300 °C, where all secondary phases are supposed to be dissolved

mechanism_principle.content: The grain refinement is caused by nucleation sites from intensive plastic deformation during milling.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This was caused by the intensive plastic deformation during high energy ball milling, which resulted in a high number of nucleation sites for new grains formed by recrystallization during SPS processing.

evidence_result.content: The specimen prepared by SPS of gas atomized powder achieved a high hardness of 410 HV10.
evidence_result.evidence_span: resulting in a high hardness of 410 HV10

evidence_result.content: The microstructure of the specimen was refined to a grain size well below 500 nm.
evidence_result.evidence_span: with grain size well below 500 nm

constraint.content: The swaging process could not be completed because the specimens cracked, preventing porosity measurement and limiting the validity of hardness data.
constraint.evidence_span: Porosity was not measured in the HEAP-S-SW specimen because the swaging process was interrupted due to specimen cracking, and the distribution of porosity was inhomogeneous.

constraint.content: Hot deformation of high-oxygen alloys is not excluded but requires specific conditions like low strain rate or high temperature.
constraint.evidence_span: It should be pointed out that the possibility of hot deformation of the alloy with increased oxygen content cannot be excluded under suitable conditions (i.e., low strain rate, or higher processing temperature)

contradiction.content: The low hardness of HEAP-HIP samples is surprising and contradicts the expectation of high entropy hardening in this material class.
contradiction.evidence_span: It has to be mentioned that HEAP-HIP and HEAP-HIP-S samples were characterized by surprisingly low hardness.
